description: Malpasset dam-break (Reyran valley, Var, France; 2 December 1959). Official TELEMAC-2D validation case. Observation set = 17 police high-water-mark survey points, 3 electrical-transformer wave-arrival (shutdown) times, and 9 downstream gauges (points 6-14) of the 1:400 LNH physical scale model.

coordinate_reference_system.note: Local coordinate system of the Malpasset study map, in metres. THIS IS THE SAME FRAME as the bundled TELEMAC mesh geo_malpasset-*.slf and the CADAM topography. Cross-check: the dam wall is a straight line between (4701,4143) and (4655,4392) in this frame (Biscarini et al. 2016, following EDF), which matches the ANUGA mesh dam nodes (4701.18,4143.41)-(4655.5,4392.10). Domain extent approx x in [0, 17300] m, y in [0, 8400] m.
coordinate_reference_system.georef_hint: Dam site is approx 43.5072 N, 6.7539 E (UTM zone 32N approx E=318435, N=4819592) per the anuga_malpasset georeferencing; this is an approximate anchor, NOT a published transform of the local frame.

vertical_reference.datum_note: Water levels are maximum free-surface ELEVATIONS in metres above the local vertical datum (Nivellement General de la France, NGF), not depths; values decrease monotonically down-valley (P1=79.15 near dam -> P17=14.0 near sea). Reservoir initial free-surface commonly cited at 100 m NGF (TUFLOW 2019). Sources do not restate the datum explicitly for every table; NGF is the standard French datum for this dataset.

provenance.numeric_source: Biscarini, C.; Di Francesco, S.; Ridolfi, E.; Manciola, P. (2016). On the Simulation of Floods in a Narrow Bending Valley: The Malpasset Dam Break Case Study. Water 8(11):545. doi:10.3390/w8110545. Tables 2, 3 and 4 (open access; fetched via Wayback Machine snapshot 2026-01-13 of the MDPI HTML).
provenance.primary_data_origin: The paper states the observed and laboratory data were kindly provided by Jean-Michel Hervouet, and cites for the gauge/point data: Morris (2000) CADAM Report SR571 (HR Wallingford) and Goutal (1999) 'The Malpasset dam failure - an overview and test case definition', 4th CADAM Meeting, Zaragoza. These CADAM/Hervouet sources are the primary origin; the MDPI paper is the open-access reproduction transcribed here.
provenance.transcription_chain: primary (Goutal 1999 CADAM / Morris 2000 CADAM SR571 / Hervouet & Petitjean 1999 JHR 37:777-788, data via Hervouet) -> reproduced in Biscarini et al. 2016 Water 8:545 (open) -> transcribed verbatim into this file. Paywalled primaries (JHR, CADAM report) were not directly accessible offline; numbers are from the open MDPI reproduction which attributes them to those primaries.

police_survey_points.quantity: surveyed maximum water surface elevation (high-water marks recorded by local police after the flood)
police_survey_points.source: Biscarini et al. 2016, Table 3 (WSobs column). Data via Hervouet.

transformers.quantity: wave arrival time inferred from electrical-transformer shutdown time after dam failure
transformers.notes: Transformer A sat just downstream of the dam; its shutdown (100 s) is taken as the reference wave-arrival time. For B and C the shutdown time lies between wave arrival and time of peak level (Biscarini et al. 2016). DISCREPANCY: TUFLOW (2019) reports transformer B recorded at 1204 s; MDPI/CADAM report 1240 s. 1240 s adopted here as primary (matches the CADAM/Hervouet dataset); 1204 s recorded as the TUFLOW variant.

physical_model_gauges.labels_note: Downstream gauges numbered 6-14 of the 1:400 scale physical model built by Laboratoire National d'Hydraulique (EDF-LNH) in 1964 (upstream gauges 1-5 are in the reservoir and not used for downstream validation). Labelled G6-G14 in the source; requested as S6-S14 - same 9 points.
physical_model_gauges.quantity: maximum water surface elevation and wave arrival time from the 1:400 physical scale model, reported at prototype (full) scale
physical_model_gauges.source: Biscarini et al. 2016, Table 4 (ATlab, WSlab columns), cited to Morris 2000 (CADAM SR571) and Goutal 1999 (CADAM).

published_model_comparison.note: NOT observations. Results of ONE published model (Biscarini et al. 2016, OpenFOAM 3D VOF RANS k-epsilon, Manning n not restated in text) reproduced here only as an additional published comparison target. Do not treat as ground truth.
